digest:
## 🔬 Major Technical Developments

### A 0-click exploit chain for the Pixel 10
URL: https://projectzero.google/2026/05/pixel-10-exploit.html
Zero-click means zero user interaction required for full device compromise
Project Zero documenting a complete exploit chain on Google's flagship device signals the ongoing cat-and-mouse game between hardware security and sophisticated attackers. This matters for any company with a mobile-first security posture or BYOD policies. The "when a door closes, a window opens" framing suggests the exploit emerged from Google's own security hardening efforts creating new attack surfaces.

### Orthrus-Qwen3: up to 7.8× tokens/forward on Qwen3, identical output distribution
URL: https://github.com/chiennv2000/orthrus
Speculative decoding breakthrough delivers nearly 8x inference speedup with zero quality loss
This is a meaningful efficiency gain for anyone running Qwen3 at scale. The "identical output distribution" claim is critical since it means production deployments can swap this in without revalidation. For infrastructure cost modeling, this moves the economics of self-hosted inference significantly closer to API pricing.

### Mini Shai-Hulud - TanStack and more npm packages compromised, with SLSA Build Level 3 provenance attestations
URL: https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem
Supply chain attack bypasses the security attestations that were supposed to prevent exactly this
TanStack is widely used across React applications. The fact that SLSA Level 3 provenance attestations were present but ineffective is the real story here. This undermines confidence in the attestation frameworks enterprises have been adopting as a defense against supply chain attacks.


## 💼 Business & Market Signals

### Power prices are up 76% on Americas biggest grid, and a watchdog is pointing fingers
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/15/power-prices-are-up-76-on-americas-biggest-grid-and-a-watchdog-is-pointing-fingers/
AI compute demand is breaking the power grid faster than it can scale
A 76% price spike on PJM (the largest U.S. grid) is a structural constraint on AI infrastructure buildout. This creates opportunity in power generation, grid modernization, and efficiency plays. Any AI infrastructure thesis needs to stress-test against power availability and pricing assumptions.

### OpenAI launches ChatGPT for personal finance, will let you connect bank accounts
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/15/openai-launches-chatgpt-for-personal-finance-will-let-you-connect-bank-accounts/
OpenAI moves from API provider to consumer fintech product with bank account access
This is a direct competitive threat to Plaid-powered fintech apps and robo-advisors. OpenAI is leveraging its distribution to expand TAM beyond enterprise API revenue. Watch for regulatory scrutiny given the sensitivity of financial data flowing through AI systems.

### Indian Uber rival Rapido raises $240M at $3B valuation
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/15/indian-uber-rival-rapido-raises-240m-at-3b-valuation/
Motorbike and auto-rickshaw ride-hailing captures Indian market dynamics Uber cannot
Rapido's model exploits vehicle economics specific to emerging markets where two-wheelers dominate. The $3B valuation at this growth stage suggests investors see a path to market leadership in India's mobility space separate from Uber/Ola.


## 📋 Case Studies & Deep Dives

### I believe there are entire companies right now under AI psychosis
URL: https://twitter.com/mitchellh/status/2055380239711457578
Mitchell Hashimoto calls out organizational dysfunction driven by AI hype
The HashiCorp co-founder's credibility makes this worth reading for diligence on any AI-native company. Pattern-match this against portfolio companies showing aggressive AI pivots with unclear technical foundations.

### SQL patterns I use to catch transaction fraud
URL: https://analytics.fixelsmith.com/posts/sql-fraud-patterns/
Practical fraud detection logic from a practitioner
Useful reference for diligence on fintech and payments companies. The specific SQL patterns reveal what signals experienced fraud analysts actually use versus vendor marketing claims.

### A Field Guide to Alternative Storage Engines for PostgreSQL
URL: https://thebuild.com/blog/2026/05/08/a-field-guide-to-alternative-storage-engines-for-postgresql/
PostgreSQL's storage layer is fragmenting into specialized solutions
This matters for infrastructure investments. Companies like Neon, Supabase, and others building on Postgres are making different storage engine bets. Understanding the tradeoffs helps evaluate their technical positioning.


## ⚡ Signal vs. Noise

The through-line today is infrastructure constraint meeting AI ambition. Power prices spiking 76%, supply chain security failing despite attestations, and a HashiCorp founder warning about organizational AI psychosis all point to the same thesis: the gap between AI capability promises and operational reality is widening. The durable opportunities are in the picks-and-shovels solving these constraints, not the companies building on assumptions that constraints will magically resolve.
